study: N2 shared edge-exit navigation, with/without communication
revision_2_note: Obstacle confound removed from the CORE study world per the root-cause audit (root_cause_audit_dynamic_heading_20260720.md); arrival latching (ARRIVED_HOLD) and two post-exit parking zones added. world_file below is now the obstacle-free core world used for PILOT04(OFF)/PILOT01(ON) onward. diagnostic_world_file preserves the ORIGINAL obstacle-containing world, still used only by the EXCLUDED_OBSTACLE_CONFOUNDED_DIAGNOSTIC pilots (PILOT01-03), never deleted.
revision_3_note: Analytic exit-geometry redesign after PILOT04-06 (all EXCLUDED_EXIT_GEOMETRY_DIAGNOSTIC, preserved). All visual markers moved to z=0.20m (empirically confirmed, via a one-time read-only sensor_ray_height_audit.sh smoke test, to be outside the e-puck ToF/IR sensor's detection height); parking-zone placement re-derived analytically (see parking_zones.clearance_analysis); max_runtime_s recomputed with an explicit one-local-encounter-resolution allowance.
revision_4_note: PILOT08 (EXCLUDED_EXIT_GEOMETRY_DIAGNOSTIC, preserved) proved revision 3's parking-zone wall clearance check was incomplete: it only verified physical/CPA-style clearance (parking_radius + robot_radius, ~0.077m), not the local IR/ToF sensor's own front_release_m-based clearance -- Robot A's parking zone at (0.6520, 0.3904) was only 0.021m from the +x wall by the physical measure, well inside front_release_m=0.220m, so Robot A's own sensor repeatedly detected the WALL ITSELF as an obstacle while trying to settle, producing an unresolvable repeating LOCAL_FRONT_WARN cycle (3+ encounters over the full 102s max_runtime_s, confirmed via controller.log TRANSITION lines) -- a wall can never be 'passed' the way local_obstacle_logic.py's SIDE_TRACK/PASS_CONFIRM maneuver resolves a discrete object, so this was a genuinely unresolvable, not merely slow, encounter. Fix: the shared exit itself relocated from (0.50, 0.50) to (0.25, 0.25) -- still clearly corner/edge-directional (not central), but with enough depth beyond it for BOTH parking zones to simultaneously clear (a) the required peer-vs-peer spacing and (b) a NEW, corrected wall-clearance check using front_release_m + robot_radius_m + geometry_margin_m (0.287m), not just physical body/marker radius. Robot A/B start poses are UNCHANGED; robot_b.search_waypoints_m's final waypoint (previously the exit's old location) is updated to the new exit center, shortening the frozen search path length and its correponding travel-time term in max_runtime_s. See parking_zones.clearance_analysis for the full recomputed numbers.
world_file_note: NEW, additive world file, obstacle-free core study world. Does not modify two_epuck_head_on_clean_world.wbt (Objective 5 A-D), two_epuck_cooperative_exit_n2_world.wbt (Stage 0), or diagnostic_world_file below.
diagnostic_world_file_note: ORIGINAL world file with the obstacle confound, revision-1 geometry. Preserved for EXCLUDED_OBSTACLE_CONFOUNDED_DIAGNOSTIC pilots only; not used by the core OFF/ON study from revision 2 onward.

exit.marker: revision 3: gate posts, the completion-zone marker, and both parking-zone markers are ALL elevated to z=0.20m (Transform nodes, purely visual) -- empirically confirmed outside the e-puck ToF/IR sensor's detection height via sensor_ray_height_audit.sh, replacing the revision-1/2 low-height (z=0-0.06m) markers that PILOT04-06 proved were being genuinely, repeatedly detected as real obstacles. Judgment region stays the same circular, software-only region (task_completion_analyzer.GoalRegion / GoalHoldTracker) it always was -- markers are cosmetic and were never load-bearing for the task logic itself, only for local IR/ToF avoidance, which is exactly what made their sensor-visibility a defect.
exit.role: single shared informational/navigation target -- both robots' current_target and Robot A's GoalAnnouncement content, common to both conditions and both robots. NOT a per-robot completion criterion as of revision 2 (see parking_zones).

sensor_ray_height_audit.method: sensor_ray_height_audit.sh + sensor_ray_height_audit_world.wbt (read-only, one-time smoke test, NOT a pilot -- no controller motion, no scoring, no bag evidence directory). A single stationary e-puck at the origin, a test marker placed 0.15m directly ahead at z=0.20m (height 0.02m box), state_publisher's fused front_distance_m read once settled.
sensor_ray_height_audit.result: front_distance_m=0.7191m, matching the far arena wall distance, NOT the 0.15m-away marker -- the elevated marker produced NO detection.
sensor_ray_height_audit.conclusion: Webots' e-puck ToF/IR DistanceSensor ray-casting IS height-selective in practice: geometry at z>=0.20m escapes detection, while low geometry (z=0-0.06m, confirmed via PILOT04-06 bag evidence: front_distance_m oscillating 0.17-1.0m+ as the robot spun in place near a gate post and separately near a parking marker, left/right staying inf) is genuinely detected. The PILOT05 hypothesis that Solid-vs-Transform node type mattered is DISPROVEN by this same evidence (ray-casting queries the rendered scene graph regardless of node type) -- height above the sensor's effective range is the actual determining factor.

other_categories_verified_by_existing_ev.wall: Genuinely detected (expected/required) -- confirmed by this same smoke test (0.7191m reading matches the RectangleArena wall distance).
other_categories_verified_by_existing_ev.other_robot: Genuinely detected (expected, by design) -- established throughout this project's controller_v4 development history (e.g. pilot_v4_b2 fusion regression, the combined box+moving-peer exclusionary pilot) and consistent with PILOT04-06's overlapping-encounter timing.
other_categories_verified_by_existing_ev.floor_marker_and_parking_marker_low_heig: Genuinely detected -- confirmed directly by PILOT05 (front_distance_m oscillation at 0.073m from a z=0.001m parking marker) and PILOT06 (0.1506m from a z=0.03m gate post).

parking_zones.note: Post-exit safe zero-velocity holding points (Part V), NOT a second task goal -- the shared exit above stays the single informational target for navigation/announcement. Each robot's goal_navigator switches current_target from the shared exit to its OWN parking point once it geometrically enters the exit region (radius exit.goal_hold_radius_m around exit center); ARRIVED_HOLD latches, and individual_completion_time_s is recorded, only once a robot continuously holds inside its OWN parking region for goal_hold_time_s. task_completion_monitor.py uses the SAME two regions so its verdict cannot disagree with either robot's own navigator.
parking_zones.revision_3_note: Analytic redesign (no further trial-and-error pilots) after PILOT04-06. PILOT04/05/06 (all EXCLUDED_EXIT_GEOMETRY_DIAGNOSTIC, preserved) proved the true root cause was NOT primarily parking-zone spacing but LOW-HEIGHT visual markers (gate posts z=0-0.06m, parking/completion markers z~0.001m) being genuinely detected by the e-puck ToF/IR ray-cast regardless of Solid vs Transform node type (a disproven PILOT05 hypothesis) -- confirmed by a one-time, read-only sensor_ray_height_audit.sh smoke test: a marker elevated to z=0.20m produced NO detection (front_distance_m read the far wall, not the 0.15m-away marker), while low markers were repeatedly detected in PILOT04-06 bag evidence. Fix: ALL visual markers (gate, completion zone, both parking zones) moved to z=0.20m in shared_exit_n2_obstacle_free_world.wbt -- purely visual, outside the sensor's detection height entirely, confirmed empirically, not assumed. Parking-zone placement independently maximized within this 1.5x1.5m arena's wall constraints (offset 0.03m past the exit center along the exit-to-corner diagonal, then split +-0.185m along the perpendicular, mirroring the gate layout) -- see robot_a/robot_b below. local_obstacle_logic.py, CPA formula, IR/ToF thresholds, safety_radius_m, and DURATION_CEILING remain untouched throughout.

clearance_analysis.parked_vs_parked_status: SATISFIED -- both robots' final resting positions clear the requirement with a 0.016m margin.
clearance_analysis.parked_vs_wall_requirement_formula: local_sensor_front_release_m(0.220) + robot_radius_m(0.037) + geometry_margin_m(0.03) -- the check MISSING in revision 3, which only verified physical/CPA-style clearance (parking_radius+robot_radius, ~0.077m) and let PILOT08's wall-triggered unresolvable encounter through
clearance_analysis.parked_vs_wall_status: SATISFIED -- both coordinates clear the corrected requirement (robot_a's tighter dimension, x, has a 0.0716m margin beyond the 0.287m requirement itself, i.e. the raw clearance is 0.287+0.0716=0.3586m > 0.287m required).
clearance_analysis.robot_b_transit_path_vs_parked_robot_a_s: NOT FULLY SATISFIED -- computed from Robot B's actual, deterministic, frozen final-waypoint approach bearing (not a worst-case any-angle bound, which is geometrically infeasible in this 1.5x1.5m arena: satisfying it simultaneously with wall clearance and parked-vs-parked spacing has no solution here). This is the best simultaneous solution found across all three constraints (parked-vs-parked, parked-vs-wall, and this transit metric); tightening this one further reopens either the wall-clearance or parked-vs-parked violation. A single, bounded local-avoidance encounter near the shared exit is therefore expected and explicitly budgeted into max_runtime_s (one_local_encounter_allowance_s, sized to the frozen local_v4_max_encounter_duration_s=25.0s DURATION_CEILING) rather than assumed away.

obstacle.note: Confirmed (verify_shared_exit_geometry.py) to intersect Robot B's waypoint search path (min distance 0.000m) and to clear Robot A's direct path (min distance 0.688m) -- asymmetric by design. Present ONLY in diagnostic_world_file (shared_exit_n2_world.wbt); removed from the core obstacle-free world (world_file) per the root-cause audit's isolation of the primary research variable (communication effect on a shared-exit task), not to force a PASS.

robot_a.role: informed -- navigates directly toward its own a-priori known exit location from t=0

robot_b.role: uninformed -- deterministic waypoint search until exit known (OFF: never; ON: upon receiving a valid GoalAnnouncement)

max_runtime_s_computation: revision 4, recomputed analytically after PILOT08's exit relocation (authorized one-time revision before the formal experiment; not to be adjusted again post-hoc). Terms: startup_hold_s(5.0) + robot_b_frozen_search_path_time_s(23.469 = 0.9388m / 0.04m/s, shorter than revision 3 because the relocated exit shortens the frozen search path) + pre_registered_turning_time_allowance_s(10.0, ~4 waypoint/handoff turns at (pi/2)/turn_rate_rps=0.65rad/s ~= 2.42s/turn, rounded up) + goal_hold_time_s(2.0) + parking_zone_transit_time_s(4.316 = 0.1726m exit-center-to-own-parking-zone distance / 0.04m/s) + one_local_encounter_allowance_s(25.0, sized to the frozen, unmodified local_v4_max_encounter_duration_s DURATION_CEILING) = 69.785s core, x1.30 (>=30% scheduling margin) = 90.72s, rounded up to 91.0s.
nominal_speed_mps_note: Overrides cooperative_avoider.py's default 0.025 via its already-declared, mutable ROS parameter -- not one of the frozen CPA formula / safety radius / local sensor threshold items. Frozen, identical OFF/ON, set before any pilot runs, never adjusted after seeing results.

off.robot_a_navigation: goal_navigator targets its own known exit location directly
off.robot_b_navigation: goal_navigator follows the frozen waypoint sequence, final waypoint is the exit itself

on.robot_a_navigation: same as OFF, plus publishes GoalAnnouncement at a bounded rate from trial start
on.robot_b_navigation: same waypoint search as OFF until the first valid, fresh GoalAnnouncement is received, then goal_navigator switches target to the announced exit location

communication.paper_note: COMM_ON combines exit-information sharing AND peer CPA coordination; the reported effect is their combined effect. No ablation isolating one mechanism from the other is run in this phase.

shared_between_off_and_on: parking_zones (both robots' own zone identical across conditions)
local IR/ToF avoidance logic and thresholds (frozen, unmodified)
